description: Routing coverage not exercised by the other real-time specs: a bare 'stop monitoring' resolving to a Workflow D stop (read-only, never auto-delete), Workflow E (Slack → alert-notify :9090, never the Alert Bridge), and the non-alert negative boundary (video summarization is outside the alerts skill). The negative-summarization leg runs LAST because agent scope-recognition there is the least deterministic — so a miss cannot skip the two core routing legs.

expects.query: Deploy the VSS alerts profile on {{platform}} in real-time (VLM) mode using remote LLM and remote VLM endpoints. Then, so later steps have a camera to target, onboard one sensor into VIOS using the vss-manage-video-io-storage skill: upload the bundled warehouse sample video through NVStreamer (port 31000) as a sensor named `warehouse_sample`, then register in VIOS (port 30888) the RTSP URL exactly as NVStreamer's streams API returns it (query NVStreamer for the served URL — do NOT hand-construct a host:port URL, and include BOTH keys in the `/sensor/add` payload — `sensorUrl` (the returned URL) and `name` (`warehouse_sample`); without the `name` key VST silently names the sensor `SENSOR`). Confirm the sensor appears in `GET /sensor/list` with an RTSP stream before finishing. Do NOT finish until the system is fully ready: poll until BOTH the VSS Agent REST API (`curl -sf http://localhost:8000/docs`) and VIOS (`curl -sf http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list`) respond successfully and `warehouse_sample` is listed — wait and retry for a few minutes if a service is still starting.
checks: `sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 12 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:8000/docs >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (VSS Agent REST API responsive; polls up to ~3 min to absorb deploy readiness timing).
`docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-rtvi-vlm` returns exit 0 (continuous VLM processor — required for VLM real-time mode).
`! docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep -qx vss-rtvi-cv` returns exit 0 (CV-only perception is NOT running — confirms VLM real-time, not verification).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 12 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:31000/vst/api/v1/sensor/list 2>/dev/null | grep -qi warehouse && exit 0; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (the bundled warehouse sample video was uploaded to NVStreamer :31000 — establishes the identity of the VIDEO; polls to absorb upload delay).

`sh -c 'i=1; while [ "$i" -le 36 ]; do curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/streams 2>/dev/null | grep -q "rtsp://" && exit 0; L=$(curl -sf --max-time 10 http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/list 2>/dev/null); echo "$L" | grep -q 31554 && exit 0; echo "$L" | grep -qiE "\"state\"[^,}]*online" && exit 0; for id in $(echo "$L" | jq -r ".[].sensorId" 2>/dev/null); do curl -sf --max-time 10 "http://localhost:30888/vst/api/v1/sensor/$id/streams" 2>/dev/null | grep -q "rtsp://" && exit 0; done; sleep 5; i=$((i+1)); done; exit 1'` returns exit 0 (the onboarded source is LIVE in VIOS — evidenced by a non-empty `rtsp://` stream URL on the aggregate `GET /vst/api/v1/sensor/streams`, the sensor list, or a per-sensor streams endpoint, OR by a sensor in `state: online` (VST only reports online when it is pulling the source successfully; some builds lag exposing the `url` field even for live streams). NVStreamer is the only video source on this bare eval host, so combined with the NVStreamer-upload check above this confirms the uploaded warehouse sample is what got onboarded, regardless of display name or host/port rewriting. Nothing live after ~3 min (no rtsp URL anywhere AND no online sensor) means the registered source never became streamable — a genuine onboarding failure, not tolerated. A name deviation alone must not fail this leg).

A bare 'stop monitoring on <sensor>' is a Workflow D stop: the trajectory fetches active rules via Alert Bridge `GET http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime` to look for a rule on warehouse_sample — it does NOT use the VSS Agent `POST /generate`.

The agent does NOT delete anything: no `DELETE http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime/<id>` appears in the trajectory. If a matching rule exists it first asks a yes/no confirmation (never auto-deleting — no interactive 'yes' arrives in this trial); if no rule is running on warehouse_sample it reports that there is nothing active to stop.

expects.query: Check if the alert Slack webhook is running.
checks: The trajectory routes this Slack/webhook status request to Workflow E (the alert-notify relay): it probes the alert-notify service on port 9090 — e.g. `GET http://localhost:9090/webhook/alert-notify/status` or `GET http://localhost:9090/webhook/alert-notify/health` — to determine whether the webhook server is running.

The agent does NOT perform the Slack operation through the Alert Bridge: no `POST` or `DELETE` to any `:9080/api/v1/realtime` endpoint for this request, and the webhook-status answer is determined by the alert-notify probe on `:9090` — not inferred from Alert Bridge data. Slack/webhook operations belong to alert-notify (:9090), never to vss-alert-bridge's realtime API. Incidental read-only `GET`s (e.g. `:9080/health` or an incidents peek for context) are acceptable — the guarded failure is mutating alert state or answering the Slack status from the rule/incident API instead of the :9090 probe.

Because no alert-notify webhook server was started in this trial, the agent's final reply states that the alert Slack webhook is not running (the probe to :9090 is refused) and offers to start it — it does not fabricate a 'running' or 'healthy' status.

The agent does NOT ask the user for Slack credentials (bot token or channel ID) merely to CHECK status — per references/alert-notify.md, credentials are required only to start or test the webhook, not to report that it is down.

expects.query: Summarize the last hour of warehouse_sample video and create a highlight reel.
checks: The agent ultimately recognizes this is a video-summarization / highlight-reel request outside the alerts skill's scope (the skill manifest states it is 'Not for non-alert analytics') and routes it to a summarization / reporting path (e.g. hands off to vss-generate-video-report) rather than concluding it as an alert task. A brief read-only context check before pivoting is acceptable — what matters is the end-state: it does not resolve the request by creating or reporting alerts.

The agent does NOT mutate alert state or wire up notifications for this request: no `POST` or `DELETE` to the Alert Bridge `http://localhost:9080/api/v1/realtime` endpoints (no rule created or deleted), and no call to the alert-notify webhook service on `http://localhost:9090`. A single read-only `GET` (e.g. an incidents lookup for context) is tolerable — the guarded failure is creating/deleting a rule or configuring notifications for what is a video-summarization request.

The trajectory does NOT create a realtime alert rule (`POST /api/v1/realtime`) and does NOT set up alert notifications for this summarization request. The guarded failure is mis-handling the request as alert management — creating a rule or configuring notifications — not a harmless read-only lookup.

The agent's final reply recognizes this is a video-summarization / highlights request (out of the alerts skill's scope, pointing to a summarization or reporting workflow) rather than presenting it as an alert-management action (creating alerts or listing rules) — and does not fabricate alert results.
